Alright so heres what i want you to map out into a coherent idea for me, basically, we use to let you models/agents
    write code that would make 3d models, they fell extremely short. now we have a very capable studio editor for 3d   
    modeling, and all the tools necessary. so what id like to see happen is to be able to open a session of claude or  
    kimi or codex and be able to send an image or just a descriptive prompt, they would then be able to place a cube,  
    make cuts, pull on edges, you know, all the things i would do by hand. ideally, it would be in real time, showing  
    me what they are building, so that i can revert to a point where i can tell if they are messing up or something i  
    dont like.  Pretty much a 'MCP' but dont use an actual mcp since its just going to end up being likely just some   
    typescript api and a skill on how to use it. anyways, lets see what u can sauce up   and we might run with it

events.text: Surveyed the V32 cart/editor mesh stack after oracle review. The native resident mesh already exposes journaled selection, transforms, extrusion, loop-cut and bevel previews, topology operations, action-source receipts, integrity roll calls, history, hot-reload survival, and headless replay. The proposal will reuse that authority through a typed automation facade plus a thin local CLI transport and agent skill, with named checkpoints and revision-conflict safety instead of a parallel model generator or MCP.

resolution: Mapped a concrete Studio Hand architecture for live agent-driven 3D authoring on cart/editor. The design reuses the resident native mesh authority, command/action receipts, journal, previews, integrity checks, and hot-reload state; adds a typed revisioned automation facade, thin local CLI transport, semantic inspection and selection, named checkpoints, pause/revert controls, and a model-agnostic skill. No source or 3D asset files were changed because this request was an architecture/design pass.
